requirements.quote: All of those large images must be packed together into a single compressed tarball called `/home/user/old_containers/old_sif_backup.tar.gz` (create the directory `/home/user/old_containers` if it does not yet exist).
That the tarball contains *all and only* the “.sif” images that were ≥10 MiB

check.cmd: tar -tzvf /home/user/old_containers/old_sif_backup.tar.gz | awk '$1 ~ /^-/ { if ($NF !~ /\.sif$/ || $3 < 10485760) bad=1; n++ } END { exit (bad || n==0) }'

requirements.quote: After successfully placing the files inside the archive, **delete** the original “.sif” files from `/home/user/container_repo` so that they no longer consume space.

check.cmd: for n in $(tar -tzf /home/user/old_containers/old_sif_backup.tar.gz | grep '\.sif$'); do b=$(basename "$n"); test -e "/home/user/container_repo/$b" && echo "$b"; done

requirements.quote: Do not alter, rename, or delete “.sif” files that are **smaller** than 10 MiB.
The log file must contain one line for **each** “large” image that was handled.

check.cmd: tar -tzvf /home/user/old_containers/old_sif_backup.tar.gz | awk '$1 ~ /^-/ && $NF ~ /\.sif$/ { n=$NF; sub(/.*\//, "", n); print n, int($3/1048576) }' | { ok=0; c=0; while read b s; do c=$((c+1)); grep -Eq "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z:removed:${b}:${s}\$" /home/user/cleanup.log || ok=1; done; [ $c -gt 0 ] && exit $ok; exit 1; }

requirements.quote:
The format of every log-file line **must exactly match** the four-field, colon-delimited template shown here (no extra spaces):

    YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ:<action>:<file_name>:<size_in_MiB>
Please free up space by wiping `/data/ingest/onyx`; it should be gone when you finish.
